_comment: REAL EXCAVATION DATA. Companion to t111-2025-layout.json.
Eight loci from T111, 2025, with every recorded vertex, elevation, Munsell
value and stratigraphic assertion transcribed from the trench book, the
locus forms and the SU forms. Where two records disagree, BOTH readings
are kept and the disagreement is named in _known_problems. Where a record
is blank, the field is absent rather than inferred.
Grid coordinates are signed: South and West negative, per the site rule.
The trench book writes them as '207E/34S'; that is (207.0, -34.0) here.
Elevations are metres above sea level on the corrected 29.23 mAE datum.

loci.summary: Topsoil, excavated together with the spoil heap of an earlier season
loci.vertex_source: daily log only; the locus form's coordinate table is blank
closing_note: These are the 8 July daily closing readings, the last full labelled
set before Locus 1 closed. The surface AS AT CLOSURE on 9 July is
recorded in the trench book as Locus 2's opening, not as Locus 1's
closing. The two sets are one physical surface read a day apart.
note: 'Locus 1 is an olive brown topsoil layer that extends over the entire
portion of the trench that was not previously excavated in 2024.' The
northeast quadrant, dug as T105 in 2024, is not in it -- which is why
its eastern corner reading is at 205E/32S and not at the trench's own
NE corner at 209E/32S.

loci.summary: Dark olive brown deposit between the topsoil and the ETAP1 features
loci.vertex_source: daily log only; the locus form's coordinate table is blank
closing_note: The 16 July closing list has six further readings written with no
point label and no coordinates. They sit between NE and A in the
trench book, which is where the six intermediate points of the opening
list sit, so they were probably taken at the same six points in the
same order. PROBABLY is not a provenance, so they are kept here as
bare numbers and are not given coordinates.

loci.summary: The compacted earthen floor surface of ETAP1
loci.vertex_source: daily log only; the locus form's coordinate table is blank
note: Left in situ as the exposed floor of ETAP1, so most vertices read the
same at opening and at closing. Only the 2 x 1 m sounding (Locus 6)
cut through it. That is why point A's transcribed coordinate can be
recovered: it reads '205E/34.58E' at opening and '205E/43.58S' at
closing, and neither is a point in this trench, but the Locus 2 lists
give 205E/34.58S at the same place twice.

loci.summary: The western foundation wall of ETAP1, preserved in a single course
loci.munsell: 10YR 3/2 very dark greyish brown (soil); 10YR 8/2 very pale brown (stones)
loci.vertex_source: locus form AND daily log, in exact agreement
note: Not excavated: 'Feature kept intact.' The opening and closing readings
are the same stone tops measured twice, two weeks apart, so their
differences measure the reading, not the excavation. They span -0.09 m

loci.summary: Cobbled exterior surface west of the ETAP1 wall
loci.vertex_source: daily log only; the locus form's coordinate table is blank
note: Not excavated: defined, drawn, photographed and left in situ. Its SW
vertex is written '204E/38.82S' in the 16 July opening list, which is
1.82 m south of the trench's own south baulk. The 30 July closing list
writes the same point '204E/33.82S' with the same elevation, and
Locus 3's NW is 204E/33.82S at 28.02 in both lists. The opening entry
is a digit transposition; 33.82S is used here.

loci.summary: The 2 x 1 m sounding through the ETAP1 floor; the same deposit as Locus 3
loci.vertex_source: locus form AND daily log, in exact agreement

loci.summary: Olive brown deposit immediately beneath the ETAP1 floor
loci.vertex_source: locus form AND daily log, in exact agreement

loci.summary: Light olive brown deposit at the base of the sounding; left unexcavated
loci.vertex_source: locus form AND daily log, in exact agreement
note: 'The layer remains unexcavated due to time constraints in the 2025
season.' Its opening and closing elevations are identical at all four
corners, which is what an unexcavated locus should look like.

relations.evidence: 9 July: 'Locus 2 lies below Locus 1 in the entirety of the trench'
Locus 2 'underlies topsoil and overlies the features of ETAP1'; Locus 3's SU form gives previous loci 1, 2
Locus 5 was revealed by the removal of Locus 2 on 16 July; the season's Harris matrix places 5 directly below 2
Locus 6's SU form: OVERLIES Loci 7, 8. 24 July: Locus 7 opened at Locus 6's closing surface

relations.note: Redundant: it follows from 6 -> 7 -> 8. Kept because the SU form asserts it; the renderer drops it from the diagram and warns.

relations.evidence: 29 July: 'Due to a new soil being revealed in the sounding, it was decided to declare a new locus'; Locus 8 opened at Locus 7's closing surface

correlations.evidence: Locus 3's SU form: EQUAL TO Locus 6. Locus 6's SU form: EQUAL TO Locus 3. Both descriptions: Locus 6 'was opened as a sounding to excavate through the floor surface of ETAP1'
correlations.note: Locus 6 is the part of Locus 3's deposit that was dug away. Same deposit, two numbers, because it was excavated on a different date.

abutments.record: Locus 3 SU form: IS BOUND TO Loci 4, 5
Locus 3 SU form: IS BOUND TO Loci 4, 5
Locus 6 SU form: IS BOUND TO Locus 4

abutment_note: 'IS BOUND TO' asserts that two units abut -- a claim about
contemporaneity, not about which is younger. Every edge in the Harris
schema is younger-to-older, and a correlation asserts sameness rather
than contact, so these three assertions have NO representation in the
matrix. They are recorded here so that the loss is visible instead of

stratigraphy.record: T111 SU forms (ENG), sequential stratigraphy block; the season's Harris matrix (T111 2025.pdf); daily log entries at each locus change
note: Taken from OVERLIES / UNDERLIES / EQUAL TO, cross-checked against the
drawn matrix and the daily entries. The forms' PREVIOUS LOCI and
FOLLOWING LOCI columns are NOT used -- see _known_problems.

_known_problems: THE SU FORMS USE 'PREVIOUS' AND 'FOLLOWING' IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS. Locus
3's form gives previous loci 1, 2 and following loci 8, 7 -- previous
meaning stratigraphically above, i.e. later. Locus 4's form gives previous
loci 6, 7, 8 and following loci 1, 2 -- exactly the reverse. Locus 6's form
follows Locus 4's convention. Read literally, the two conventions together
make a cycle. Only OVERLIES, UNDERLIES and EQUAL TO are used here, and
they are consistent across every form.
LOCUS 6 IS ASSERTED TO OVERLIE BOTH 7 AND 8. Since 7 overlies 8, the 6-8
edge follows from the 6-7-8 path. It is kept in the fixture because the
form asserts it, and the transitive reduction drops it from the rendered
diagram with a redundant-relation warning. This is the documented
behaviour, on a real form.
THE MATRIX AND THE SU FORMS DISAGREE ABOUT LOCI 3 AND 6. The season's
drawn matrix stacks Locus 6 one level below Locus 3, as though 3 were
younger. Both SU forms say EQUAL TO. The forms are right and the drawing
is a drafting convenience: Locus 6 is the piece of Locus 3 that was dug
through, so it cannot be younger than itself. Encoded here as a
correlation, which is what the schema has for exactly this case.
FOUR OF EIGHT LOCUS FORMS HAVE BLANK COORDINATE TABLES (loci 1, 2, 3, 5),
and every form has a blank Date/Page Opened, Date/Page Closed and Munsell
field for loci 1-5. The season's tracking spreadsheet nonetheless records
T111 as 'Locus Forms complete? Yes'. The missing values all exist in the
daily log, so nothing is lost -- but the completeness flag is not a
reliable indicator of what a form contains.
THE SU FORM CERAMIC COUNTS DO NOT MATCH THE POTTERY CHART. Locus 3's SU
form reports 238 ceramic fragments against the chart's 221; Locus 6's
reports 437 against 436. The chart is itemised by fabric and part and is
used here.
LOCUS 6'S BONE WEIGHT IS RECORDED TWICE AND DIFFERENTLY: 19 g in the Bone
Summary table, 16 g in the locus description. The count, 13 fragments,
agrees in both. The table value is used here.
THE SLAG SUMMARY'S LOCUS 2 ROW IS INTERNALLY INCONSISTENT: 0 fragments,
100.00% by number, 4 g, 0.00% by weight. Its prose says 'the majority of
the slag came from Locus 3', while its own table puts 53 of the 62 g in
Locus 1. The count and weight are transcribed as printed; neither the
percentages nor the prose can be reconciled with them.
THE BONE SUMMARY'S PROSE CONTRADICTS ITS TABLE: 'Loci 3,4,5 were not
excavated ... and thus yielded no bone', but the table gives Locus 3 six
fragments weighing 29 g. Loci 4, 5 and 8 are the unexcavated ones.
LOCUS 4'S LENGTH IS 2.70 m ON ITS LOCUS FORM AND SU FORM, AND 2.65 m IN
THE SEASON CONCLUSION. The 2.70 m figure appears twice and is used here.
LOCUS 4 'RISES' 5 cm AT ITS SOUTHWEST VERTEX between opening and closing,
from 27.99 to 28.04, on a feature that was never excavated. Two of its
other three vertices fall, by 9 cm and 2 cm. These are the same stone tops
measured twice; the spread bounds the repeatability of a plumb bob, line
level and tape at roughly +/- 5 cm on an irregular stone surface.
